output.title: Known issue: dashboard slow to load with 10,000+ rows
output.content: Dashboards with more than 10,000 rows currently load slowly because pagination is not yet applied server-side. Workaround: filter the dashboard by date range to reduce the row count. A server-side pagination fix is on the roadmap but has no committed release date.

output.title: API rate limits
output.content: The API allows 100 requests per minute on the Free and Pro plans, and 1000 requests per minute on the Enterprise plan. Exceeding the limit returns an HTTP 429 response with a Retry-After header.

output.title: Data export / GDPR requests
output.content: To request a full export of your account data for GDPR or personal record-keeping purposes, go to Account Settings > Privacy > Request Data Export. The export is prepared within 30 days and sent as a download link to your account email.

steps.rawOutput:
Thank you for reporting this issue. Based on our records, we have a known issue where dashboards load slowly when handling large datasets due to pagination not yet being applied server-side. While your dashboard with 500 rows is below the threshold where this issue typically becomes most pronounced (it primarily affects dashboards with 10,000+ rows), the underlying performance limitation could still be affecting your experience.

Unfortunately, the standard workaround of filtering by date range doesn't seem to be helping in your case. To better understand what's causing the 30-second load time on your smaller dataset, we'll need to investigate further. This may involve factors specific to your dashboard configuration or data structure.

I'd recommend reaching out to our support team with details about your dashboard setup (such as the types of visualizations, number of columns, or any custom calculations) so we can look into this more thoroughly. We do have a server-side pagination fix on our roadmap that should resolve these performance concerns, though there's no committed release date yet.
